description: GeoRisk Explorer is an Earth-observation and geospatial analytics project focused on environmental change in the Lower Piura basin, Peru. We use satellite and climate datasets to examine rainfall and land-surface trends, map historical flood extent, and explore spatial exposure. I bring Python, GIS, remote sensing, data analysis, and machine learning. I’m open to collaborators in Earth science/hydrology, statistics, web development, UX/design, and science communication.
summary: GeoRisk-Explorer is an experimental geospatial AI workflow designed to map flood-affected areas using Sentinel-1 satellite radar imagery. It combines the Sen1Floods11 v1.1 HandLabeled dataset with TerraMind v1 Base and a U-Net decoder for binary water segmentation. The prototype includes quantitative model evaluation, qualitative prediction analysis, and reproducible geospatial workflows. Its intended application is territorial flood research in Bajo Piura, Peru, with Catacaos as a proposed pilot area. The project provides a foundation for integrating hydroclimatic observations and territorial exposure analysis into future flood intelligence systems. Long-term Earth system trend detection and statistical significance testing remain future development tasks.
details:
GeoRisk-Explorer implements a Python-based geospatial machine learning pipeline for flood-water segmentation.

The current experimental configuration uses Sen1Floods11 v1.1 HandLabeled data, Sentinel-1 VV/VH imagery, and a pretrained TerraMind v1 Base encoder combined with a U-Net decoder.

The model was evaluated on 86 validation samples using a global pixel-level confusion matrix. The reported Flood IoU was 0.7003, Water Dice was 0.8237, Water Precision was 0.8273, and Water Recall was 0.8201.

The project includes modular Python components, YAML experiment configurations, training and validation reports, and qualitative prediction visualizations.

The research focuses on the potential application of satellite-derived flood information to territorial analysis in Bajo Piura, Peru, including Catacaos as a proposed pilot area.

The current prototype demonstrates flood segmentation and model evaluation. Long-term Earth-system trend analysis and statistical significance testing remain planned extensions.
